To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DPT cell population was increased in patients with TB as compared with healthy individuals.
the DPT cells were increased in PBMCs of patients with TB, and the levels of DPTs were gradually decreased down upon pharmacotherapy.
DPT cells are a subset of T cells that express both CD4 and CD8, and that they play an important role in protective immunity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and function of DPT cells and the alterations in peripheral blood of tuberculosis patients during the period of phar-macotherapy.
the role of DPT cells during the period of pulmonary TB.
the role and significance of CD4＋ CD8＋ double-positive T cells in the pathogenesis of tuberculosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study has demonstrated that DPT cells play an important role in the protective immunity of pulmonary tuberculosis.

the study has provided a better understanding of the role of CD4＋ CD8＋ T cells in the immune response against Mtb infection, but further investigations are needed to determine the exact mechanism by which these cells contribute to the control of TB.
the CD4＋CD45RO＋CD25＋CD8＋ T cells are the main effector cells in the peripheral blood of patients suffering from tuberculosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DPT cells in the peripheral blood of patients are increased and the levels of CD25 and cytokines in DPT cells are also increased, and the DPT cells are memory cells.
we have identified a new type of T cells, CD4＋CD28＋CD8＋（ DPT） cells, which are present in peripheral blood and in lymphoid organs of healthy individuals.
we found that CD4＋CD 8＋ double positive T cells （DPT cells） were significantly elevated in the peripheral blood of the TB patients and the DPT cells were activated T cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the DPT cells in patients with TB are a novel type of T cell with a high capacity of producing IFN-γ and TNF-α, and the alterations of DPT cell levels in peripheral blood during the period of treatment may be an indicator for the prognosis.
the double-positive T cells are not a rare population in the peripheral blood of tuberculosis patients.
CD4＋CD 8 ＋T cells are involved in protective immunity against TB and the alteration of CD4＋ CD8＋T in PBMCs is an indicator for the prognosis and treatment of pulmonary tuberculosis.
